text: Ryanair announced plans to cut 1 million passenger seats in Spain, which sounds like a capacity reduction until you see the maintenance crew rolling out the chainsaws and asking passengers if they'd like to stand for the two-hour flight to Madrid.

The Nazi-looted painting finally resurfaces after 80 years in hiding. But not for long—the museum just announced a three-year closure for renovations, and it will spend that time in a climate-controlled warehouse in New Jersey.
The government's spotlight on childcare arrived Tuesday as actual spotlights. Daycare workers report the 500-watt bulbs have helped them see their funding shortage much more clearly.

Experts weigh in on body wipes and confirm they work by successfully converting "I smell like a gym bag" into "I smell like a gym bag that's trying." This counts as a win in the personal hygiene community.

The show documents her quest for privacy through exclusive interviews, intimate home footage, and a camera crew that lived with her family for six months. Netflix has already renewed it for two more seasons.

Some universities now allow pets in student housing to help with stress and anxiety. The fish are particularly effective since students can now watch something else struggle to stay afloat in an unnatural environment.

Taipei bought a Chinese-made patrol robot to catch rule-breakers, but now the council itself is under investigation for the purchase. Turns out the fastest way to join your robot in the dog house is to be the one who brought it home.

Bureau of Meteorology reports severe storm is doing continuous barrel rolls towards the south because it's the only weather system that failed its atmospheric navigation exam twice and has to take the "scenic route."

Nonalcoholic beer can help people stay sober, but it's not for everyone. It completely fails people who've built their entire personality around craft beer snobbery and need the actual alcohol to justify being insufferable about hops. Without the ABV, you're just paying nine dollars for bitter water while boring everyone stone-cold sober.
Massachusetts is converting cranberry bogs into vibrant wetlands. The bogs have reportedly filed paperwork to officially change their career from "juice ingredient" to "frog apartment complex."

After their U.S. Open match, Jelena Ostapenko and Taylor Townsend got into a heated post-match row about whether grunting on serve should follow an A-flat or B-flat pitch. Officials report both players then demonstrated their preferred frequencies for over ten minutes.

That free sample program where we all inhale 68,000 microplastic particles a day is honestly the most generous I've ever seen. Usually you have to give them your email and pretend you might buy the full-size version.
